summary: Same pattern family — per-pixel independent pale-blue twinkles on black, no spatial motion, no modes — but the port's twinkle cadence is ~3.4x too fast and frame-rate-coupled (dark gaps median 0.10 s vs the original's 1.20 s, scaling exactly as 1/fps), its peak colour is ~50% more saturated, and its envelope lacks the original's full-brightness plateau.
observations: Both sides compile and run clean (no compileError/runtimeError), on the default strip rig of 60 px. Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both). Neither side exposes ANY control: meta.json control lists are empty on orig and port, and --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for both — so the control surfaces match and there are no dials to compare.

Genre match: on a 60 px strip both render a black background with per-pixel independent twinkles. Waterfalls on both sides are pure vertical dashes — no horizontal slope, no travelling feature. Neighbour lit-state agreement is at chance on both sides (orig 0.481 for adjacent pixels vs 0.547 at lag 17; port 0.566 vs 0.604), i.e. no spatial correlation on either side. Per-pixel mean brightness is uniform along the strip (orig 58.7..119.2, port 79.2..118.7 over 60 s), so no pixel is favoured on either side.

No regime/mode structure on either side. A 240 s / 5 fps survey is homogeneous top-to-bottom for both; brightnessTrend 'steady' on both in the 60 s and 240 s surveys; a --skip 120 late window reproduces the same statistics as t=0..60 (orig onsets 0.189 vs 0.196 /px/s, port 0.602 vs 0.673). Both sides start from black at t=0 and reach steady state within ~1 s; no warm-up transient on either.

COLOUR (from --dump, not the images): the original's twinkles are a single fixed colour that peaks at exactly RGB (204,206,255) — 11,639 identical peak samples in a 60 s dump, one chroma ratio 0.80/0.81/1.00 — i.e. HSV hue 0.660, saturation 0.20, value 1.0. The port peaks at ~(178,195,254) / chroma 0.70/0.77/1.00 — hue 0.629, saturation 0.30. Both sides are single-hue (99-100% of lit samples fall in one 15-degree hue bin), so the port has the right idea but is ~50% more saturated and slightly cyan-shifted: side by side the original reads pale lavender-white and the port reads steel blue. Confirmed identical across seeds 1/7/1234, all fps, all rig sizes.

ENVELOPE (pixel-0 waveform at 20 fps, values are max-channel): original = 5-frame ramp 30,93,161,219,255 (~0.25 s), then a HARD PLATEAU at 255 for ~7 frames (~0.35 s), then exponential decay 234,210,186,164,143,...,3,0. Port = a smooth 10-frame S-curve rise 21,58,101,143,180,209,231,245,253,254 (~0.5 s) with NO plateau, then a smooth decay. The original's twinkle therefore 'pops' to full and holds; the port's rounds over its peak.

PEAK AMPLITUDE: every single original event reaches full brightness — over 1,800 threshold-crossing events in a 60 s dump, the peak percentiles are p05=p25=p50=p75=p95=255. The port's peaks are ragged: p10=143 at 60 px, and at 12 px the MEDIAN peak falls to 143 with p10=21, because port events are repeatedly cut to 0 mid-rise/mid-decay by an immediate retrigger (visible in the raw series as '...251 244 234 0 0 21 58 101...').

CADENCE — the headline divergence (default 60 px rig, 20 fps, 60 s, ~1,800-2,400 events per side, reproduced on seeds 1, 7, 1234 and in the late window): the original's pixels go properly dark between twinkles — onset rate 0.196/px/s, dark-gap median 1.20 s, mean 1.82 s, p90 4.20 s, with a broad roughly-exponential gap distribution (only 13% of gaps under 0.25 s, 7.9% over 5 s). The port's onset rate is 0.673/px/s (3.4x) with dark-gap median 0.10 s, mean 0.41 s, and 80% of all gaps under 0.25 s — i.e. the port's LEDs essentially never turn off, they dip for 2 frames and re-ignite. Lit fraction is similar (orig 0.624, port 0.698) and mean brightness is close (orig 73, port 81 over 60 s), so the divergence is in the RHYTHM, not the density.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING (measured from --dump gap durations, not from the saturating `motion` stat): the port's dark-gap median is 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.05 s at 10 / 20 / 40 fps — an exact 1/fps law, i.e. the retrigger is a per-FRAME probability. The original's is 1.50 / 1.20 / 1.00 s over the same 4x fps change (mostly time-based, mild residual coupling), and its onset rate is flat at 0.196 / 0.196 / 0.199 per px/s while the port's climbs 0.441 / 0.673 / 0.775. On real hardware running faster than 20 fps the port degrades further toward a continuous boil.

Both sides' DECAY is time-based and matches in kind but not in rate: the per-second decay factor is fps-invariant on both (orig 0.0501 / 0.0491 / 0.0479 at 10/20/40 fps; port 0.118 / 0.113 / 0.119), giving time constants of ~0.33 s (orig) vs ~0.46 s (port) — the port's tails linger ~40% longer. Both attacks are time-based at ~0.5 s (attack+plateau frames 5/11/22 orig, 5/10/20 port at 10/20/40 fps).

RIG SCALING DIVERGES (non-default rigs, stated as such): the original's spawn budget is a fixed whole-strip rate — back-solving observed onsets against available dark pixels gives ~30 spawn attempts/s at 12 px, 60 px and 300 px alike, so the strip length sets the density. At --pixels 12 the original is therefore nearly saturated (lit fraction 0.97, mean brightness 162, waterfall is broad near-white plateaus with occasional dark) while the port at 12 px strobes hard (lit fraction 0.668, mean brightness 63, onset rate 3.108/px/s, 100% of dark gaps under 0.25 s, median peak only 143) — the two are unrecognizable as the same pattern on a short strip. At --pixels 300 they converge again (orig lit 0.160 / mean 16, port lit 0.205 / mean 21) though the port still shows 35% of gaps under 0.25 s vs the original's 2%.

Stochastic character is seed-robust on both sides: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give orig onset rate 0.196/0.206/0.202 and gap mean 1.82/1.58/1.67 s; port 0.673/0.679/0.657 and 0.41/0.38/0.44 s. Neither side is a one-seed fluke, and the port/orig gap ratio is stable at ~4x across all three.

No periodicity on either side: per-pixel value autocorrelation decays monotonically from lag 1 with no secondary peak out to 6 s on both sides, confirming both are genuinely stochastic rather than a phase-offset deterministic wave.
feedback: Retrigger cadence is the main fix. On a 60 px strip at 20 fps the original leaves each pixel fully dark for a median 1.20 s (mean 1.82 s, p90 4.2 s, broad exponential spread, only 13% of gaps under 0.25 s) between twinkles; the port's median dark gap is 0.10 s with 80% under 0.25 s. Slow the port's spawn/retrigger by roughly 3.4x at the default rig so individual LEDs visibly rest between sparkles instead of flickering continuously.

The port's spawn rate is frame-counted, not time-based: its median dark gap is exactly 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.05 s at 10 / 20 / 40 fps while the original's onset rate is flat at ~0.196 per pixel per second across all three. Scale the spawn probability by elapsed time per frame so the twinkle rate is fps-independent — otherwise fixing the rate at 20 fps will leave it wrong on hardware running faster.

Peak colour: the original peaks at exactly RGB (204,206,255) = hue 0.660, saturation 0.20, value 1.0. The port peaks at (178,195,254) = hue 0.629, saturation 0.30. Desaturate the port by about a third and nudge the hue up slightly (~0.63 -> ~0.66); the target is a pale lavender-white, not a steel blue.

Envelope shape: the original ramps to full in ~0.25 s, HOLDS at full brightness for ~0.35 s, then decays with a ~0.33 s time constant, and every twinkle reaches full (peak = 255 at all percentiles over 1,800 events). The port rises smoothly over ~0.5 s with no plateau and decays with a ~0.46 s constant. Add the flat-top hold at full brightness, sharpen the attack, and shorten the decay tail by ~40% — the original's sparkle is a crisp 'pop and hold', the port's is a soft bell.

Stop truncating twinkles: the port frequently cuts an in-flight event to 0 mid-rise or mid-decay and immediately restarts it (raw series show '...251 244 234 0 0 21 58...'), which is why 10% of its events never exceed brightness 143. The original never zeroes an in-flight twinkle; when it retriggers a lit pixel it restarts the ramp from a non-zero level. Let each twinkle finish, or at least avoid the hard drop to black.

Spawn budget vs strip length: the original spawns a roughly FIXED ~30 twinkles per second across the whole strip regardless of pixel count, so a 12 px strip ends up 97% lit (a near-solid pale glow) and a 300 px strip only 16% lit. The port does not follow the same law — at 12 px it strobes (lit fraction 0.668, median peak 143) where the original is nearly solid. Make the spawn rate a whole-strip total rather than a per-pixel probability so short and long strips behave like the original's.

Everything else already matches and should be preserved: black background with exact-zero off pixels, single-hue twinkles, zero spatial correlation between neighbouring pixels, uniform density along the strip, no modes or long-period drift over 240 s, and seed-robust statistics.
